subject: Tenant localization certification & certified purge checklist request
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <amoreno@finsecure.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: confirmation of tenant locality + certified purge artifacts for Dedicated cluster

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As part of our procurement checklist we need a short Q&A and a set of artifacts for your Dedicated deployment that will host FinSecure workloads. Can you confirm the following at a tenant level:

- Whether a customer can request a "site-local only" pin at deployment creation and have all runtime data (model inputs, logs, KV cache, snapshots, backups) restricted to that region/availability zone.
- Whether automated snapshots/backups are ever copied outside the pinned region (including warm/DR buckets).
- Exact retention windows for primary data and backups, and the deletion workflow for both (timeline and proof).
- The certified purge process: what artifacts do you provide when we request a tenant wipe (signed manifest, job logs, snapshot hashes, operator attestations)?

We also need an example runbook describing the tenant-scope wipe and an estimate for how long a full certified purge takes from request to delivery of artifacts. If you can send a short matrix and a proposed checklist we can use for legal/infosec signoff, that would be ideal.

Copying our auditor, Gina Park, for evidence requirements.

Regards,
Alex
Director, Platform Security
FinSecure Inc.

Attachments: none

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: confirmation of tenant locality + certified purge artifacts for Dedicated cluster

Alex —

Thanks, this is straightforward to answer. Summary up front: yes — we support region-only tenancy for Dedicated at provisioning; backups and snapshots are configurable to be region-local; and we produce a signed certified-purge package that includes a job manifest, per-object checksums, node reimage logs, and a signed attestation.

Deliverables I will provide in an artifact bundle:
- locality_matrix_v1.xlsx (breaks down every data class and where it can exist by configuration)
- wipe_runbook.pdf (technical runbook for tenant-scope purge)
- sample_signed_manifest.json (example of the post-wipe artifact)

Open questions from our side that will change timelines:
1) Will your legal hold require backup retention beyond our standard backup TTL (30 days)? If yes, we need to schedule an escrow/retention exception before cutover.
2) Do you require HSM-backed key deletion evidence (customer-managed KMS) or is a provider-managed KMS acceptable?

I’ve looped Ben and Vanessa for the technical and ops details. We can assemble the bundle and a short acceptance checklist within 3 business days once the scope (backs beyond 30 days, escrow) is confirmed.

Proposed next step: 30-minute gate call tomorrow to align on the acceptance checklist and whether we need a retention exception. When is good for you?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <amoreno@finsecure.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T08:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: confirmation of tenant locality + certified purge artifacts for Dedicated cluster

Alex —

Happy to provide the technical breakdown. Key points (concise):

1) Region pinning at create time
- For Dedicated, the tenant's compute and persistent storage are bound to the selected region and AZs at provisioning. We create region-scoped VPCs, storage buckets, and node pools.

2) Snapshots/backups replication
- Default behavior: automated snapshots and backups are kept in region-scoped storage (same region) only. Cross-region replication is off by default.
- Optional: cross-region replication can be enabled by request (used only for disaster recovery) and requires documented agreement (we will record this in the locality matrix).

3) Retention windows and deletion workflow
- Primary runtime data: ephemeral caches purged on session end; KV caches sized for 24 hours TTL by default.
- Persistent customer data (objects, logs): default TTL 90 days for logs, 30 days for snapshots/backups.
- Deletion workflow: when a tenant requests a purge we run a tenant-scoped wipe job that:
  a) takes tenant offline and prevents new writes,
  b) zeroes and deletes tenant objects from the storage layer,
  c) triggers node reimage for compute nodes that served the tenant,
  d) runs a glacier sweep to remove indexed references and any queued replication jobs,
  e) generates a signed manifest and per-object sha256 checksums, and
  f) hands the artifact package to the customer.
- Typical completion estimate: 6-10 hours for a small-medium tenant (no cross-region replication); 24-72 hours if cross-region artifacts or third-party snapshot exports exist.

4) Certified purge artifacts we provide
- signed_manifest.tar.gz (list of deleted objects, timestamps)
- per_object_sha256.csv
- node_reimage_logs.tar.gz (operator logs showing reimage and image checks)
- audit_attestation.pdf (operator-signed statement, timestamped)

5) Keys and HSMs
- If you use customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key via KMS), we can coordinate a KMS key deletion call and include KMS deletion receipts in the artifact bundle. If you rely on provider-managed keys, we provide an internal key-lifecycle snapshot and deletion log.

I attached the operational runbook (wipe_runbook.pdf) for your security and infra teams to review. If legal hold applies, Ben noted we will need a retention-exception workflow (escrow) to preserve backups in an isolated escrow bucket until release.

- Ben
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: wipe_runbook.pdf (type: document)

From: Alex Moreno <amoreno@finsecure.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Gina Park <gina@auditsolutions.io>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: confirmation of tenant locality + certified purge artifacts for Dedicated cluster

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from Infosec and Legal:

- Our legal hold policy may require that certain backups be retained for up to 1 year in an escrow state. Can you confirm if you support an escrow bucket architecture (isolated, read-only, no cross-region replication) and the controls you enforce around access?
- For the signed_manifest we would like a PGP-signed artifact in addition to the internal attestation PDF so our tooling can automatically verify integrity. Can you produce that?
- For KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys (we have an AWS KMS with an offline key rotation plan). Please confirm the process to coordinate key material deletion and how you confirm the key state to us as part of the purge package.

Last: please confirm whether backups that are stored for >30 days are excluded from automatic scrub and whether the escrow bucket will be included in your certified purge unless we explicitly request an escrow release.

If you can capture these clarifications in the acceptance checklist and provide a call window Monday morning PST, we can move to the next stage.

—Alex

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <amoreno@finsecure.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T16:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: confirmation of tenant locality + certified purge artifacts for Dedicated cluster

Alex —

Thanks — short answers and next steps below. I pulled together the acceptance checklist and a small set of example artifacts; links are in related_links.

1) Escrow bucket: yes, we support an isolated escrow bucket in the pinned region. Controls: read-only policy, dedicated service account, restricted IAM to a named set of engineers, MFA-protected release workflow, and no cross-region replication. Escrow buckets are treated as separate objects for purge: we will not include them in an automated purge unless the customer explicitly authorizes release of escrow.

2) Signed manifest: we can produce both a provider-signed attestation (PDF) and a PGP-signed manifest file. We will include the public key fingerprint in the artifact metadata.

3) KMS coordination: we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) and will schedule a key deletion coordination call. The purge package will include KMS deletion receipts (request IDs) and a timing log showing the key state transitions. If you require an HSM export certificate we can produce the KMS key-change audit with the HSM vendor integration notes.

4) Backups >30 days: by default those are excluded from automatic scrub only if placed into escrow. If you elect escrow, backups are immutable and will be kept until a documented release event. They will not be included in the standard tenant purge unless you issue a separate release instruction.

Next steps I propose:
- I will send the artifact bundle (locality matrix, runbook, and sample signed manifest) after this thread.
- Please confirm whether you want escrow for the legal-hold set. If yes, reply with the list of retention IDs and we will provision escrow buckets and update the acceptance checklist.
- I’ll set a 30-minute call Monday 09:00 PST to walk the acceptance checklist and the DocuSign attestation.

Thanks — will share the DocuSign/attestation link and HubSpot ticket in a follow-up (see related_links).

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
